comments.content: The batched update uses `Promise.all` over `context.globalState.update` calls. VS Code's `Memento.update` is not guaranteed to be safe under concurrent writes to the same underlying storage — batching via `Promise.all` may cause race conditions or lost writes. Consider serializing with a sequential loop, or verify that the VS Code API guarantees atomicity per key. The same concern applies to `updateSecretsBatch`.

`updateGlobalStateBatch` accepts `Record<string, any>` and casts keys to `GlobalStateKey` without validation. If a caller passes a key not in `GlobalStateKey`, TypeScript won't catch it. Consider typing the parameter as `Partial<Record<GlobalStateKey, any>>` to preserve type safety.

`updateSecretsBatch` accepts `Record<string, string | undefined>` and casts to `SecretKey`. Same type-safety concern as `updateGlobalStateBatch` — prefer `Partial<Record<SecretKey, string | undefined>>`.

The comment says 'Batch all global state updates into 2 operations instead of 47' but the batched object contains 20 + 29 = 49 keys (the original code had 20 ephemeral + 27 global = 47). The count in the comment is inaccurate; also the '2 operations' claim is misleading since `Promise.all` still issues N individual `update` calls, just concurrently. Please correct the comment to avoid confusion.
The log message hardcodes 'was ~535ms, now should be <50ms'. This is a stale/aspirational claim that will be misleading in production logs. Remove the hardcoded comparison or make it dynamic.

Multiple `[PERF]` console.log statements were added throughout `getAllExtensionState` and `updateApiConfiguration`. These will fire on every state read/write and could be noisy in production. Consider gating them behind a debug flag or removing them before merge.
Debug `[PERF]` logging added here (and throughout this file) will run on every provider switch in production. Consider gating behind a debug flag or removing before merge.
Frontend `[PERF]` logging added here will fire on every field change in the settings UI. Consider gating behind a debug flag or removing before merge.

`backdropFilter: blur(8px)` is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (provider switching performance). It also has inconsistent browser support in VS Code webviews (Electron/Chromium should be fine, but this is a visual change that should be in its own PR). Please split this out.
